The Fermat point minimizes the sum of distances from a point to the vertices of a polygon. For a convex pentagon with angles of \( 60^\circ \), the Fermat point is the point where the angles between the lines connecting the point to the vertices are all \( 120^\circ \).

The Fermat point for a pentagon can be found by constructing equilateral triangles on the sides of the pentagon and connecting the vertices of these triangles to the opposite vertices of the pentagon. The intersection of these lines is the Fermat point.
